title: Mastery
coreMove: Mastery grows when challenge, feedback, and a growth mindset turn effort into progress without pretending perfection arrives.

exampleSpecs.audience: Silas, a piano teacher setting a stretch target
exampleSpecs.stakes: A student needs challenge without panic.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the edge between boredom and overwhelm.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ari, a coding coach turning weakness into practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: A code review could shame a learner or create a useful drill.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use deliberate practice on a concrete weakness.

exampleSpecs.audience: Daphne, a simulation lead calibrating difficulty
exampleSpecs.stakes: A surgical simulation is either too easy to teach or too hard to learn from.

exampleSpecs.audience: Hugo, a language tutor reframing errors
exampleSpecs.stakes: A learner may treat mistakes as proof of lacking talent.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use growth mindset as a practical response.

exampleSpecs.audience: Cleo, a coach selecting one film clip
exampleSpecs.stakes: An athlete needs one reachable improvement instead of a pile of criticism.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn feedback into the next stretch.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ruth, a speaking coach scheduling a repeat
exampleSpecs.stakes: A speaker needs feedback quickly enough to revise.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Close the practice loop with immediate repetition.
